title: Boss: The Tip Calculator
story: The Bug Wasp bet that you cannot build a working calculator. Prove it wrong.
goal: On click of #calc: read #bill and #pct (percent), then show the tip with 2 decimals in #tip as Tip: 12.50, and the total in #total as Total: 112.50. If #bill is empty or not a number, show Enter a bill in #tip and clear #total.

tests.label: 100 at 12.5% gives 12.50
tests.js: type("#bill","100"); type("#pct","12.5"); click("#calc"); return (txt("#tip") === "Tip: 12.50" && txt("#total") === "Total: 112.50") || txt("#tip") + " / " + txt("#total")

tests.label: 80 at 10% gives 8.00
tests.js: type("#bill","80"); type("#pct","10"); click("#calc"); return (txt("#tip") === "Tip: 8.00" && txt("#total") === "Total: 88.00") || txt("#tip") + " / " + txt("#total")

tests.label: Empty bill is rejected
tests.js: type("#bill",""); type("#pct","10"); click("#calc"); return (txt("#tip") === "Enter a bill" && txt("#total") === "") || txt("#tip") + " / " + txt("#total")

tests.label: Text is rejected
tests.js: type("#bill","abc"); type("#pct","10"); click("#calc"); return txt("#tip") === "Enter a bill" || txt("#tip")

tests.label: A blank percent counts as 0
tests.js: type("#bill","50"); type("#pct",""); click("#calc"); return (txt("#tip") === "Tip: 0.00" && txt("#total") === "Total: 50.00") || txt("#tip") + " / " + txt("#total")

tests.label: The script runs with no errors

hints: Check the bill first with isNaN, and return early.
toFixed(2) gives two decimals as text. total = bill + tip.
socratic: What does parseFloat return for text?
What happens if you skip the early return?
Why toFixed(2) and not rounding yourself?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Boss: The Tip Calculator”?
